Article title: CAR T-cell therapy for B-cell lymphoma.
Study objective: To review the use and clinical outcomes of FDA-approved anti-CD19 CAR T-cell products in patients with indolent or aggressive B-cell lymphomas, including mechanisms of treatment failure and potential strategies to address them.
Main finding: Anti-CD19 CAR T-cell therapy has produced unprecedented and durable responses in high-risk, relapsed or refractory B-cell lymphomas and is now a standard treatment after two or more prior lines of therapy for aggressive B-cell lymphoma.
Relevance to research question: The article directly evaluates CD19-targeted CAR T-cell therapy in B-cell malignancies and supports CD19 as an effective therapeutic target, but it does not directly compare CD19 with alternative targets.

Article title: CAR T-Cell Therapy in Hematological Malignancies.
Study objective: To review the application of CAR T-cell therapy in different hematological malignancies and strategies to overcome CAR T-cell dysfunction and improve efficacy.
Main finding: CD19 is the most commonly targeted antigen on B-cells and has been predominantly used to treat lymphoma and acute lymphocytic leukemia, resulting in approval of five CAR T-cell therapies. CAR T-cell treatment remains more difficult in other malignancies such as acute myeloid leukemia.
Relevance to research question: The review directly discusses CD19 as the predominant CAR T-cell target in B-cell malignancies and its clinical success, but it does not directly compare CD19 with alternative targets to determine whether it is superior.

Study objective: To review the use, efficacy, safety, challenges, and emerging developments of chimeric antigen receptor T-cell therapy for B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma, including CD19-targeted CAR-T cells.
Main finding: CD19-targeted CAR-T cells produce robust and durable responses in heavily pretreated patients with several B-cell malignancies, but treatment is associated with CRS, ICANS, cytopenias, infections, and secondary malignancies. Alternative CAR targets and armored CARs are under development.
Relevance to research question: The article supports CD19 as an effective target for B-cell malignancies but does not directly compare CD19 with alternative targets or establish that it is superior.

Article title: Blinatumomab in pediatric B-acute lymphoblastic leukemia.
Study objective: To synthesize selected literature on clinical trials of blinatumomab in pediatric relapsed or refractory B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia, focusing on determinants of efficacy and treatment-related adverse events.
Main finding: Blinatumomab provides substantial short-term clinical benefits and tolerability in pediatric relapsed or refractory B-ALL, but its efficacy is influenced by tumor burden, T-cell function, CD19 antigen loss, and lineage switch; cytokine release syndrome, neurotoxicity, and infections require close monitoring.
Important limitation: The long-term impacts of blinatumomab in pediatric patients require further investigation.
Relevance to research question: The review is directly relevant because blinatumomab targets CD19 and discusses CD19 antigen loss as a determinant of treatment efficacy in B-cell malignancy. However, it does not compare CD19 with alternative targets or establish that CD19 is superior.
